Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred while the other vehicle was changing lanes. The reported
mechanism is consistent with the shoulder complaints documented at intake, and the injury pattern is plausible for a impact of
this type. Over the course of 29 visits, care followed a conventional progression, beginning with physical therapy,
range-of-motion work, and home exercise instruction, then tapering in frequency as symptoms improved and strength returned.
Physical examination revealed limited abduction and tenderness over the rotator cuff insertion, findings that support the clinical
diagnosis, while several neurological screens and imaging-independent stability tests returned normal results. The patient reports
no prior injury or treatment to this shoulder, and no earlier records addressing this body region were identified in the chart
review. Billing reflects one charge per scheduled service, with no dulpicate or repeated entries. At discharge the patient had
reached a stable functional level with residual mild stiffness, and continued home exercise was recommended.
